'''Wolfgang Fink''' is a German-American theoretical physicist.<ref name="SPIE, the international society for optics and photonics 2023 n146">{{cite web | title=Wolfgang Fink: The 2023 SPIE Aden and Marjorie Meinel Technology Achievement Award | website=SPIE, the international society for optics and photonics | date=January 11, 2023 | url=https://spie.org/news/wolfgang-fink-the-2023-spie-aden-and-marjorie-meinel-technology-achievement-award?SSO=1 | access-date=December 14, 2023}}</ref> He is currently an associate professor and the inaugural Maria  & [[Edward Keonjian]] Endowed Chair of Microelectronics at the [[University of Arizona]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://directory.arizona.edu/phonebook|title=Phonebook|date=June 14, 2023|website=UA Directory}}</ref>  Fink has joint appointments in the Departments of Electrical & Computer Engineering,<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 19, 2011 |title=Wolfgang Fink |url=https://ece.engineering.arizona.edu/faculty-staff/faculty/wolfgang-fink}}</ref> Biomedical Engineering,<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 11, 2012 |title=Wolfgang Fink |url=https://bme.engineering.arizona.edu/faculty-staff/faculty/wolfgang-fink}}</ref> Systems & Industrial Engineering,<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 28, 2020 |title=Wolfgang Fink |url=https://sie.engineering.arizona.edu/faculty-staff/faculty/wolfgang-fink}}</ref> Aerospace & Mechanical Engineering,<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 18, 2013 |title=Wolfgang Fink |url=https://ame.engineering.arizona.edu/faculty-staff/faculty/wolfgang-fink}}</ref> and Ophthalmology & Vision Science<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://eyes.arizona.edu/profile/wolfgang-fink-phd|title=Wolfgang Fink, PhD &#124; Ophthalmology Department|website=eyes.arizona.edu}}</ref> at the University of Arizona. He is the current Vice President of the Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) Society.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Officers |url=https://phmsociety.org/about-the-prognostics-and-health-management-society/officers/ |accessdate=December 22, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=December 23, 2020 |title=Wolfgang Fink Named VP of Prognostics and Health Management Society |url=https://ece.engineering.arizona.edu/news-events/wolfgang-fink-named-vp-prognostics-and-health-management-society}}</ref>

==Research career & education==
Fink has a B.S. (Vordiplom, 1990) and M.S. (Diplom 1993) degrees in [[physics]] and [[physical chemistry]] from the [[University of Göttingen]], Germany, and a Ph.D. ''"summa cum laude"'' in [[theoretical physics]] from the [[University of Tübingen]], Germany (1997).<ref name="Electrical and Computer Engineering 2011 b399">{{cite web | title=Wolfgang Fink | website=Electrical and Computer Engineering | date=October 19, 2011 | url=https://ece.engineering.arizona.edu/faculty-staff/faculty/wolfgang-fink | access-date=December 14, 2023}}</ref><ref name="Stoltz 2023 a036">{{cite web | last=Stoltz | first=Michael | title=Scientist Wolfgang Fink to Outline Mars Cave & Lava Tube Exploration & Comms during Mars Society Convention | website=The Mars Society | date=July 18, 2023 | url=https://www.marssociety.org/news/2023/07/18/scientist-wolfgang-fink-to-outline-mars-cave-lava-tube-exploration-comms-during-mars-society-convention/ | access-date=December 14, 2023}}</ref> He was a senior researcher at [[NASA]]'s [[Jet Propulsion Laboratory]] (2001–2009). He was also a visiting associate in [[physics]] at the [[California Institute of Technology]] (2001–2016),  where he founded Caltech's Visual and Autonomous Exploration Systems Research Laboratory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Welcome to the Visual and Autonomous Exploration Systems Research Laboratory |url=http://autonomy.caltech.edu/main.html}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Visual and Autonomous Exploration Systems Research Laboratory &#124; |url=https://www.vaesrl.com/ |website=www.vaesrl.com |accessdate=December 22, 2021}}</ref> He also held  concurrent appointments as Voluntary Research Associate Professor of both [[Ophthalmology]] and Neurological Surgery at the [[University of Southern California]] (2005–2014).

==Active research areas==
Fink is a specialist in the areas of autonomous systems, biomedical engineering for healthcare, human/brain-machine interfaces, and smart service systems. In particular, his research focuses on autonomous robotic systems for hazardous environments, C<sup>4</sup>ISR architectures ([[Tier-Scalable Reconnaissance]]), vision prostheses for the blind, smart mobile and tele-ophthalmic platforms, ophthalmic instruments and tests, self-adapting wearable sensors, cognitive/reasoning systems, and computer-optimized design.

Fink was a principal investigator of the [[United States Department of Energy]]'s ([[USDOE]]'s) ''"Artificial Retina"'' project<ref>{{Cite web |title=About the Artificial Retina Project |url=http://artificialretina.energy.gov/about.shtml |access-date=February 6, 2017 |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304064010/http://artificialretina.energy.gov/about.shtml |url-status=dead }}</ref> (2004–2011), a multi-institutional and multi-disciplinary CRADA-based effort to develop an implantable microelectronic retinal device that restores useful vision to people blinded by retinal diseases ([[Retinitis pigmentosa]] and [[Macular degeneration]]). Furthermore, Fink is [[Caltech]]'s founding Co-Investigator of the [[National Science Foundation|NSF]]-funded [[Center for Biomimetic Microelectronic Systems]] (2003–2010), awarded in 2003 to [[University of Southern California]], [[Caltech]], and [[UC Santa Cruz]]. The center enacted the only [[FDA]]-approved visual prosthesis to date ([[Argus retinal prosthesis]] or ARGUS II).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.energy.gov/articles/fda-approves-first-bionic-eye-blind|title=FDA Approves First Bionic Eye for the Blind}}</ref>

==Honors & awards==

* Fellow of the National Academy of Inventors (NAI), Class of 2023<ref name="Rittenhouse 2023 u969">{{cite web | last=Rittenhouse | first=Rebekah | title=NAI Announces 2023 Class of Fellows | website=NAI | date=December 12, 2023 | url=https://academyofinventors.org/nai-announces-2023-class-of-fellows/ | access-date=December 14, 2023}}</ref> for having ''"demonstrated a highly prolific spirit of innovation in creating or facilitating outstanding inventions that have made a tangible impact on the quality of life, economic development, and welfare of society"''.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Two UArizona faculty elected to the National Academy of Inventors|date=December 11, 2023 |url=https://news.arizona.edu/story/two-uarizona-faculty-elected-national-academy-inventors}}</ref>
* Recipient of the 2023 [[SPIE]] Aden and Marjorie Meinel Technology Achievement Award ''"for pioneering, sustained contributions to the development of transformational opto-medical examination and device technologies, with particular focus on visual prostheses for the blind, ophthalmology, and tele-ophthalmology."''<ref name="SPIE, the international society for optics and photonics h051">{{cite web | title=SPIE Aden and Marjorie Meinel Technology Achievement Award | website=SPIE, the international society for optics and photonics | url=https://spie.org/about-spie/spie-awards/spie-aden-and-marjorie-meinel-technology-achievement-award?SSO=1 | access-date=December 14, 2023}}</ref>
* Co-winner of [[USDOE]]/[[NREL]]-sponsored E-ROBOT Prize 2021 (Phase 1: $200,000),<ref>{{Cite web |title=E-ROBOT Prize |url=https://americanmadechallenges.org/EROBOT/ |website=americanmadechallenges.org |accessdate=December 22, 2021}}</ref> an American-Made Challenge, to devise building envelope retrofit solutions that make retrofits easier, faster, safer and more accessible for workers. The ''team "wall-EIFS"'' co-led by Fink devised ''"wall-EIFS: a robotically applied, 3D-sprayable exterior insulation and finish system (EIFS) for building envelope retrofits."''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.herox.com/EROBOT/round/817/entry/35682|title=Submission|website=www.herox.com}}</ref>
* Recipient of the inaugural ''Scott Clements Most Valuable Person (MVP) Award'' of the Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) Society (2020).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bios and Descriptions of PHM Society Contributors |url=https://phmsociety.org/phm-society-awards/bios-and-descriptions-of-phm-society-contributors/ |accessdate=December 22, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=November 30, 2020 |title=Fink Receives PHM Society's Inaugural Scott Clements MVP Award |url=https://ece.engineering.arizona.edu/news-events/fink-receives-phm-society-inaugural-scott-clements-mvp-award}}</ref>
* [[ARVO]] Fellow, Class of 2023.<ref name="The Association for Research in Vision and Ophthalmology e822">{{cite web | title=ARVO Fellows Class of 2023 | website=The Association for Research in Vision and Ophthalmology | url=https://www.arvo.org/awards-grants-and-fellowships/arvo-fellows/2023-ARVO-Fellows/ | access-date=December 14, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Vision Society Adds Forward-Looking Professor to 2023 Class of Fellows |date=December 2022 |url=https://news.engineering.arizona.edu/news/vision-society-adds-forward-looking-professor-2023-class-fellows}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Fink Selected as Fellow of Vision Research Association |date=December 14, 2022 |url=https://ece.engineering.arizona.edu/news-events/fink-selected-fellow-vision-research-association}}</ref>
* Fellow of [[SPIE]] (inducted in 2020) ''"for achievements in vision science for the blind and tele-ophthalmic healthcare worldwide"''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://spie.org/profile/Wolfgang.Fink-50917?SSO=1|title=Wolfgang Fink|website=spie.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=January 21, 2020 |title=SPIE Selects Wolfgang Fink as 2020 Fellow |url=https://news.engineering.arizona.edu/news/spie-selects-wolfgang-fink-2020-fellow}}</ref>
* Fellow of the Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) Society (inducted in 2018).<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 29, 2018 |title=The Key to Healthy Humans, Safe Spacecraft and Prospering Plants |url=https://news.engineering.arizona.edu/news/key-healthy-humans-safe-spacecraft-and-prospering-plants}}</ref>
* ACABI Fellow 2017 recognizing ''"faculty that are strongly active in innovation related to ACABI"'', the Arizona Center for Accelerated BioMedical Innovation at the [[University of Arizona]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 2, 2018 |title=Wolfgang Fink Named ACABI Fellow for Biomedical Research and Advancements |url=https://bme.engineering.arizona.edu/news-events/wolfgang-fink-named-acabi-fellow-biomedical-research-and-advancements}}</ref>
* da Vinci Fellow 2015 for ''"innovative, productive and highly recognized engineering research"'' at the [[University of Arizona]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 7, 2014 |title=Wolfgang Fink Named da Vinci Fellow for 2015 |url=http://news.engr.arizona.edu/news/wolfgang-fink-named-da-vinci-fellow-2015}}</ref>
* Senior Member [[IEEE]]
* College of Fellows of the [[American Institute for Medical and Biological Engineering]] (AIMBE) (inducted in 2012) ''"for outstanding contributions in the field of ophthalmology and vision sciences with particular focus on diagnostics and artificial vision systems"''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://aimbe.org/college-of-fellows/cof-1416/|title=Wolfgang Fink, Ph.D. COF-1416 – AIMBE}}</ref>

==Patents==
Fink has been awarded 31 US and international patents to date in the areas of autonomous systems, biomedical devices, neural stimulation, MEMS fabrication, data fusion and analysis, and multi-dimensional optimization.<ref name="Justia Patents Search 2016 k411">{{cite web | title=Wolfgang Fink Inventions, Patents and Patent Applications | website=Justia Patents Search | date=June 6, 2016 | url=https://patents.justia.com/inventor/wolfgang-fink | access-date=December 14, 2023}}</ref>
